lines.text: Survey ship Centaur. Day 212 of a long, quiet survey of the Greyan Drift.

lines.speaker: Lt. Sato
lines.text: Captain, we're picking up a signal. Old Greyan encoding, repeating.

lines.speaker: Chief Castell
lines.text: A distress call? Out here? Someone's alive on that derelict.

lines.speaker: Chief Castell
lines.text: With respect, Captain, regulations say we render aid. The crew will expect it.

lines.speaker: Lt. Sato
lines.text: And if it's a lure? Greyan ships don't just go quiet.

lines: Castell's jaw tightens. He isn't used to losing an argument.

lines.speaker: Dr. Voss
lines.text: The derelict is the Greyan ship Ilsk. Dead for decades, if the hull scans are right.

lines.speaker: Husk
lines.text: And yet it is transmitting, Captain. Something aboard still has power.

lines.speaker: Chief Castell
lines.text: Greyan drive tech is worth more than this whole ship. If there's anyone to save, we save them. If there isn't...

lines.speaker: Lt. Sato
lines.text: If there isn't, we leave it alone.

choices.label: Sato's right. Scan it from here first.

lines.speaker: Dr. Voss
lines.text: No life signs. Just that signal, over and over.

lines.speaker: Husk
lines.text: And a data core, Captain. Still warm.

lines: There's no avoiding it. Someone has to go over.

lines.text: The shuttle has room for two.

lines.speaker: Lt. Sato
lines.text: Nobody's home. Look at the dust on everything.

lines.speaker: Lt. Sato
lines.text: Captain, this console... someone's patched a relay into it. Recently. That's our hardware.

lines: While you pull the data core, Sato pockets a tap from the relay: a log of every message sent through it.

lines.speaker: Chief Castell
lines.text: Look at this place. The drive core's fully intact. We'd be rich.

lines: While you pull the data core, Castell wanders over to the comms console. He comes back a little too quickly.

lines.speaker: Chief Castell
lines.text: Nothing over there. Let's go.

lines.speaker: Dr. Voss
lines.text: The core is Greyan, all right. And that signal isn't a distress call.

lines.speaker: Dr. Voss
lines.text: It's a warning. 'Do not take what sleeps here.' Their drive core is unstable. It killed them.

lines.speaker: Dr. Voss
lines.text: Captain, I'd like to keep this between us until I'm sure. If the crew panics...

choices.label: No. The crew deserves to know.

lines.text: Ship's night. The bridge lights are dimmed to amber.

lines.speaker: Husk
lines.text: Captain. I have found something I do not like.

huskReport.speaker: Husk
lines: Someone altered the navigation log at 0300. Our course now runs to the Ilsk's drive core, and from there to a Free Trader depot.
The change was made with a command code. I cannot see whose.

lines.text: Morning. Someone aboard means to take the Centaur. You have time to talk to your crew.

choices.label: Ask Husk for a status report.

talkSato.speaker: Lt. Sato

lines.text: That relay tap we pulled? I decoded it. Messages to a Free Trader depot, signed with a security cipher.

lines: Only one department aboard uses that cipher, Captain.

talkSato.speaker: Lt. Sato

lines.text: You listened to me before, so I'll say it. Castell's been in the comms bay every night this week.

lines: I copied his last transmission. Here.

talkSato.speaker: Lt. Sato

lines.text: I told you that signal was a trap. Now someone's playing games with our course.

lines: Ask Castell where he was at 0300. I'd love to hear his answer.

talkCastell.speaker: Chief Castell

lines.text: Captain. Rough night?

lines: If someone's been at the nav log, my money's on the synthetic. Husk can get into everything.

lines.speaker: Chief Castell
lines.text: Asleep. Ask anyone.

lines: You do ask. Nobody saw him.

talkVoss.speaker: Dr. Voss

lines.text: Thank you for keeping quiet. I've confirmed it: take that drive core, and it kills everyone within a light-minute.

lines: Whoever changed our course knows that. Or doesn't care.

talkVoss.speaker: Dr. Voss

lines.text: You told them about the warning. Fine. Then they know, and someone changed our course anyway.

lines: That isn't ignorance, Captain. That's greed.

lines.text: All systems nominal. Except for the crew, who are not.
Engine output steady. Someone keeps checking the shuttle's fuel. It is not me.
I have traced the command code used on the nav log. It belongs to the security office.
You call the senior staff to the bridge. Every eye is on you.

lines.speaker: Chief Castell
lines.text: Well, Captain? You say someone's planning a mutiny. Who?

choices.label: Chief Castell. You changed our course.
Husk. You can get into everything.
Dr. Voss. You hid the warning.

lines.speaker: Chief Castell
lines.text: You can't prove a thing.

lines.speaker: Lt. Sato
lines.text: Relay tap. Nav log. Command-code trace. We can.

lines.speaker: Husk
lines.text: Chief Castell, you are relieved of duty. I will escort you.
With ${evidence.count} pieces of evidence on the table, the brig door closes on Castell.
The Centaur turns away from the Ilsk, and leaves it sleeping.

lines.speaker: Dr. Voss
lines.text: Let it sleep. Some things should stay lost.

lines.speaker: Chief Castell
lines.text: ${mutiny.accused}? Really?
While the crew argues, Castell's people take the shuttle bay. By ship's night, the Centaur is his.

lines.speaker: Chief Castell
lines.text: Nothing personal, Captain. That drive core is worth more than all of us.
Weeks later, a Free Trader depot vanishes in a flash bright enough to see from three systems away.

lines: You order the Centaur away from the Ilsk at full burn.

lines.speaker: Lt. Sato
lines.text: Course laid in. Whatever's on that ship can stay there.

lines.speaker: Chief Castell
lines.text: ...Aye, Captain.
You never learn who changed the course. But some nights you catch Castell watching the stars behind you.
